title: A Verdict for the Will
premise: Yara Okonkwo, archivist of St. Brannoc's Cathedral, has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidents, earning her a reputation among the town's wary insiders. When the diary of missing parishioner Edith Marsh surfaces in the crypt and its entries continue for weeks after her disappearance, Yara realizes Edith may be alive — or that someone is forging entries to bury a fourth crime. Her investigation collides with Father Ambrose, her mentor, whose loyalty to the cathedral's founding families has cost him his honesty. To expose the truth, Yara must find Nell Pryce, the witness everyone swears died in the flood of 1979, before the spring tide gives up what it took from the drowned crypt. In the end, Nell testifies, Ambrose confesses to decades of cover-ups, and Yara chooses truth over belonging, leaving the cathedral with the verdict she wrote herself.
about_author: Coral Okafor is a former parish records clerk who spent six years cataloguing centuries of baptisms, burials, and quiet scandals in English coastal towns. She writes mysteries about the documents people leave behind and the truths institutions prefer to lose.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. While cataloguing flood-damaged ledgers in the locked crypt, Yara finds Edith Marsh's diary wedged behind a reliquary — three weeks after Edith vanished. The final entry names a name Yara recognizes. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She compares the diary's handwriting against Edith's donation letters and confirms it's genuine — yet the entries continue past the disappearance date. Detective Sergeant Hale dismisses her again. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being believed by no one.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Researching the 1979 flood that sealed the lower crypt, she learns a woman named Nell Pryce was declared dead though no body was recovered. Emotional beat: the first thread pulled loose from a very old knot.

chapters.title: Father Ambrose's Kindness
chapters.summary: Ambrose's POV. He notices Yara's questions about the crypt and gently steers her toward safer work, revealing his own knowledge of the flood through a slip he immediately regrets. Emotional beat: affection shadowed by concealment.

chapters.title: Three Deaths, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She revisits her three earlier 'accidents' — the verger, the stonemason, the solicitor — and maps them against dates in Edith's diary. Each death followed an entry mentioning Nell Pryce. Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At a memorial tea, she probes the Vane and Ashcombe descendants who fund the cathedral. Their warmth curdles when she mentions the flood. Emotional beat: the realization that belonging here has always been conditional.

chapters.title: A Room That Isn't on the Plans
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following measurements that don't add up in the 1890s blueprints, she locates a bricked chamber off the lower crypt. Behind fresh mortar, a smell of salt and old paper. Emotional beat: vertigo at the threshold.

chapters.title: Hale Draws a Line
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Under pressure from above, Hale warns Yara off officially but privately admits the three cases were closed too fast. He gives her one redacted file. Emotional beat: an ally who can only afford to be one in the dark.

chapters.title: Edith's Last Walk
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reconstructing Edith's final known evening, Yara traces her to the sea wall below the cathedral and finds a hidden niche where someone could pass messages for years. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger becoming personal.

chapters.title: The Diary Continues
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A new entry appears in the diary while it sits in Yara's own locked office — written in Edith's hand, dated yesterday. Someone has access to everything. Emotional beat: fear turning inward; nowhere is neutral ground.

chapters.title: Nell Pryce, Alive Somewhere
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A retired ferryman recalls a scarred woman who took the night boat for years under another name. Yara sends a letter to the last address on his memory. Emotional beat: hope handled like something breakable.

chapters.title: Ambrose Breaks Slightly
chapters.summary: Ambrose's POV. Confronted with the opened chamber, Ambrose half-confesses: the founding families paid the cathedral to keep the flood's dead 'at rest' — and some of the dead were never dead. He begs her to stop. Emotional beat: love and betrayal in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Vane Vault
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Breaking into the Vane family vault records, she finds burial certificates signed by Ambrose for people with no graves. One signature belongs to Nell Pryce — dated after her death. Emotional beat: fury sharpening into method.

chapters.title: Someone Follows the Archivist
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Watched through the cloisters, then run off the road near the sea wall, Yara survives because the tide timing saves her. She keeps the cracked windshield rather than report it. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into stubbornness.

chapters.title: What Edith Knew
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Decoding the diary's liturgical calendar references, Yara understands Edith had been passing evidence out of the chamber for months — and that the 'accidents' were silencings. Edith didn't vanish; she hid. Emotional beat: admiration for the missing woman.

chapters.title: The Reply
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A postcard arrives with no words except a tide table and a date: the spring equinox. Nell is alive and will surface only when the water does. Emotional beat: cautious joy, quickly armored.

chapters.title: Ashcombe's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marianne Ashcombe's POV. The family matriarch offers Yara funding, position, and protection if the diary disappears. Marianne believes she is saving the cathedral, not damning it. Emotional beat: self-deception dressed as duty.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Tide
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Hale agrees to meet her at the sea wall at dawn; Ambrose, torn, leaves the crypt key in her door. Yara writes her own account of all four deaths and seals it — insurance. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: Spring Equinox
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At low tide the sea gives up the chamber's outer passage, and Nell Pryce walks out of the mist — old, scarred, and carrying forty years of documents. But they are not alone; a car's lights sweep the shingle. Emotional beat: awe laced with imminent danger.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Buried
chapters.summary: Yara and Nell's alternating POV. Pursued through the flooded passage, they escape as Hale arrives; the attacker is revealed as the cathedral's warden, the founding families' enforcer across four deaths. Emotional beat: survival bought at the edge of drowning.

chapters.title: A Verdict for the Will
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. With Nell's testimony and Edith's diary, the inquest reopens; the warden is charged, the Ashcombes' charity collapses, and Ambrose resigns, asking nothing but her forgiveness. Yara gives him honesty instead of absolution. Emotional beat: justice without comfort.

chapters.title: What the Archivist Keeps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Months later, Yara catalogs the reopened crypt honestly, including its crimes, and mails Edith's diary back to the woman herself, alive under a new name. She stays in the town — on her own terms now. Emotional beat: belonging redefined as chosen, not granted.
